question: How will the Commission ensure that every product sold to EU consumers through an online platform has a verified and genuinely accountable economic operator established in the EU?

Where no accountable EU-based operator or seller can be traced by authorities, will the Commission ensure that the online platform facilitating the sale assumes responsibility for compliance with applicable EU product rules in order to protect children and businesses in the EU?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.11.2026) With the upcoming European Product Act (EPA) proposal, the Commission plans to ensure that in the case of products sold in the EU, including through online channels, there will be an economic operator established in the EU that can be traced back and which will need to fulfil the relevant statutory compliance tasks.
Depending on the case, this may be the manufacturer, the importer, the authorised representative, or another relevant operator under the applicable EU product legislation.

The EPA proposal aims to close accountability gaps and strengthen enforcement of the rules by introducing an identification and verification system that builds on the existing Digital Product Passport framework1, and that allows for the demonstration of compliance.

In the context of the EPA, the Commission is also considering whether the obligations on providers of online marketplaces are commensurate with the role they play in the supply chain. Any such measures need to remain coherent with the existing EU legal framework, including the Digital Services Act2 (DSA).
Enforcement action by the Commission under the DSA has already led to fines on Temu (EUR 200 million) and AliExpress (EUR 550 million), and proceedings are ongoing against Shein.
